we introduce Attention Inforced Mixed Language Training for zero shot cross lingual task orientated dialogue systems and that it outperforms existing methods.

(1) we introduce Attention Inferred Mixed Language Training (A-MLT), a novel approach to adapt cross lingual task-oriented dialogue systems to low-resource languages using very few word pairs; (2) A-MLT leverages attention scores to automatically select source words and generate code switching sentences; and (3) A-ML-T significantly improves the performance of zero-shot adaptation in both dialogue state tracking and language understanding tasks

a small number of word pairs are sufficient to enable zero shot learning for low resource languages.
a small amount of bilingual data is sufficient for cross lingual dialogue systems to achieve zero shot adaptation performance.
